AC11 explanatory defeat remains even if this schedule passes: lowering b changes preference labels but supplies no informative new hard-feasible mechanism.

Zero-impact clip dominance survives both b=1 and b=0. The new local schedule does not rescue AC11 from its no-opening defeat condition.

J03/J07 imply 4 retention beginning boundary 3, removal by boundary 9, and optional H restoration boundary 10. Hold demand, timing, identities, capacities, exclusivity, and one operator fixed. Compare only impact preference b=2,1,0: received two-pin has 2 impacts and qualifies only at 2; received clip/sleeve and fresh head-loop have 0 impacts and qualify at all three. Hard feasibility is unchanged by b. Adjacent b=0 retains this same schedule without additional relaxation. Q_theta remains unknown in {0,4}; this route does not use Q. No physical execution, equal-search comparison, mechanically opened mechanism, or global novelty is established.

operation_trace.action: Fix impact preference as the sole ladder variable and distinguish preference eligibility from hard feasibility.
operation_trace.result: Setting -> mechanisms -> usefulness/cost map: b=2 ordinary: pin, clip, sleeve, and head-loop qualify; b=1 assigned: clip, sleeve, and head-loop qualify, pin does not; b=0 adjacent: the same zero-impact mechanisms qualify, pin does not. All four remain mechanically hard-feasible in every setting. Received costs: pin 4 actions/2 impacts, clip 2/0, sleeve 6/0 restored or 5/0 release-only. Fresh head-loop predicts 6/0 restored or 5/0 release-only. The activation threshold is b=2 for pin preference qualification, with no mechanical activation threshold caused by b. Usefulness of zero-impact routes remains, and clip has lower action burden. Received replay is upstream finite-model evidence; fresh route and adjacent-setting statements are modeled projections.

operation_trace.action: Construct one head-loop candidate and specify a separating replay probe using unchanged action rules.
operation_trace.result: Probe the listed actions at b=1, then relabel the identical replay at b=0: record retention at each required tick, resource occupancy, removal boundary, action count, and tap count. Hard-valid and preference-satisfied are separate outputs. Against received two-pin, retention remains 4 while impacts differ 0 versus 2; pin qualification should change only across b=2 to b=1. Against clip, both qualify across all settings but head-loop consumes four more actions when H is restored. An observed hard-feasibility change caused solely by b would contradict its stipulated soft status; unchanged mechanisms support AC11 defeat rather than a novelty claim.
